saints.name: St. Adelaide
saints.title: Empress
saints.shortBlurb: A queen imprisoned and delivered, empress of the Romans, who in widowhood gave herself to peace-making and the poor…
biography: Born in 931, the daughter of Rudolph II, king of Burgundy, and Bertha of Swabia, Adelaide was married at sixteen to Lothair, king of Italy, and left a widow within three years. The usurper Berengar II, seeking to force her into marriage with his own son, imprisoned her in 951; escaping, she was delivered by Otto the Great of Germany, who married her at Pavia that same year.

Crowned empress with Otto at Rome in 962, she shared his care for the Church, and after his death in 973 guided the realm as mother of Otto II and, from 991, as regent for her grandson Otto III. A friend of Cluny and its reform, she founded and endowed monasteries — among them Selz in Alsace — and spent her influence on the peace of the realm and the relief of the poor.

Retiring to her monastery of Selz, she died there on 16 December 999 and was canonized by Urban II in 1097. Crowned in a second marriage and once a prisoner for refusing a third, she is fittingly invoked as patroness of brides, of widows, and of second marriages.
saints.knownFor: Holy Roman Empress and benefactress of the Church.

canonization.canonized: Canonized in 1097 by Pope Urban II

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 16 December
